edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Age nunc, omnes erraverint; deceptus sit Apostolus de testimonio reddendo quibusdam; nullam respexerit Spiritus Sanctus, uti eam in veritatem deduceret, ad hoc missus a Christo, ad hoc postulatus de Patre, ut esset doctor veritatis; neglexerit officium Dei villicus, Christi vicarius, sinens Ecclesias aliter interim intelligere, aliter credere, quam ipse per Apostolos praedicabat: ecquid verisimile est, ut tot ac tantae in unam fidem erraverint? Nullus inter multos eventus unus est exitus: variasse debuerat error doctrinae Ecclesiarum. Caeterum, quod apud multos unum invenitur, non est erratum, sed traditum. Audeat ergo aliquis dicere illos errasse qui tradiderunt?
pass_a_gloss: Now come, let all have erred; let the Apostle have been deceived about giving testimony to certain people; let the Holy Spirit have looked back at no one, so that He might lead that one into truth, sent for this purpose by Christ, requested for this purpose from the Father, so that He might be the teacher of truth; let the steward of God, the vicar of Christ, have neglected his duty, allowing the Churches to understand and believe otherwise meanwhile, than what He Himself was preaching through the Apostles: is it likely that so many and such great ones have erred into one faith? There is not one outcome among many events: the error of the doctrine of the Churches ought to have varied. Meanwhile, what is found to be one among many is not something that has been erred, but something that has been handed down. Therefore, let someone dare to say that those who handed down erred.
pass_b_english: Come now — suppose they all erred. Suppose the Apostle was deceived in his testimony to certain people. Suppose the Holy Spirit never glanced back to guide the Church into truth, despite being sent by Christ for that very purpose, requested from the Father for that very purpose, to be the teacher of truth. Suppose the steward of God, the vicar of Christ, neglected his duty, letting the churches meanwhile understand and believe something other than what he himself preached through the apostles. Is it plausible that so many and such great churches would have erred their way into a single faith? Among many events there is not a single outcome: the error of the churches' doctrine should have varied. Yet what is found to be one across many is not error — it is tradition. So let someone dare to claim that those who handed it down were mistaken.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the subjunctive mood of the hypothetical argument ('suppose/let...'). Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Latin text. Pass B's use of 'suppose' for the subjunctive 'erraverint', 'deceptus sit', etc., is a valid stylistic choice for the rhetorical structure. All clauses, including the complex description of the Holy Spirit's mission and the steward's duty, are preserved.
